newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU sets special status for German regional banks-sources.
newsitem.headline: EU sets special status for German regional banks-sources.

text.p: European Union leaders have agreed to give Germany's regional public banks (Landesbanken) special status in a resolution to be attached to the new EU treaty, German government sources said on Tuesday.
The deal was struck at the mid-year summit of EU leaders in Amsterdam.

The sources said that under the agreement, the EU recognised that the Landesbanken carried out in part public tasks and their special financial status should therefore remain exempt from the EU's competition rules.
The Landesbanken have been involved in a long-standing dispute with Germany's commercial banks, which accuse them of distorting competition due to public support.
The dispute became more heated when the German government recently proposed to exclude banks from EU treaty provisions bannking public subsidies which harm fair competition.

The proposal was made within the framework of the inter-governmental conference (IGC) to reform the EU treaty ahead of the bloc's expansion eastwards. Any revision of the treaty required the unanimous approval of all 15 states.
The German sources said Germany had won support from all the other 14 member countries for the new resolution on Tuesday.
